```{r}
#| label: data-results
#| include: false

load(file = here("input/data/proc/df_final.RData"))

# Index of the three original subjective social status measures (own, family of
# origin and children), with its WE/BE decomposition. Used as a control in the
# models that include the trajectory slope.
df_study1 <- df_study1 %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(sss_index = rowMeans(across(c(ess, ess_og, ess_hijos)))) %>%
  group_by(idencuesta) %>%
  mutate(sss_index_mean = mean(sss_index, na.rm = TRUE),
         sss_index_cwc  = sss_index - sss_index_mean) %>%
  ungroup()

df_model <- df_study1 %>%
  na.omit()
names(df_study1)

# N of observations and persons used in a figure -----------------------------

# single variable (or set of variables jointly non-missing)
n_note <- function(vars, data = df_model) {
  d <- data %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(vars), ~ !is.na(.x)))
  paste0("N = ", format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), " observations, ",
         format(n_distinct(d$idencuesta), big.mark = ","), " persons")
}

# correlation matrices (pairwise-complete): range of N across variable pairs
n_note_pw <- function(vars, data = df_model) {
  d <- data %>% ungroup()
  n <- combn(vars, 2, simplify = FALSE) %>%
    map(function(p) {
      dd <- d[complete.cases(d[, p]), ]
      c(obs = nrow(dd), per = n_distinct(dd$idencuesta))
    }) %>%
    do.call(rbind, .)
  rng <- function(x) {
    if (min(x) == max(x)) format(min(x), big.mark = ",")
    else paste0(format(min(x), big.mark = ","), "-", format(max(x), big.mark = ","))
  }
  paste0("N = ", rng(n[, "obs"]), " observations, ",
         rng(n[, "per"]), " persons")
}

# data of the i-th wave (waves are ordered 2016, ..., 2023)
wave_data <- function(i, data = df_model) {
  data %>% ungroup() %>% filter(ola == sort(unique(ola))[i])
}
```

# Descriptives

## Social Subjective Status (SSS)

```{r}
#| label: fig-ess-dist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of subjective social status (own, family of origin and children) by wave"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-align: center

ess_labs <- c(ess = "Own", ess_og = "Family of origin", ess_hijos = "Children")

df_ess <- df_model %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ola, all_of(names(ess_labs))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ola, names_to = "var", values_to = "val") %>%
  filter(!is.na(val)) %>%
  mutate(var = factor(var, levels = names(ess_labs), labels = ess_labs)) %>%
  count(var, ola, val) %>%
  group_by(var, ola) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

df_ess_mean <- df_model %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ola, all_of(names(ess_labs))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ola, names_to = "var", values_to = "val") %>%
  mutate(var = factor(var, levels = names(ess_labs), labels = ess_labs)) %>%
  group_by(var, ola) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(val, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(df_ess, aes(x = val, y = prop)) +
  geom_col(fill = met.brewer("Hiroshige", 1, direction = -1)[1], width = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(data = df_ess_mean, aes(xintercept = m),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), n.breaks = 3) +
  facet_grid(ola ~ var) +
  labs(x = "Subjective social status (0 = lowest, 10 = highest)", y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Dashed line: wave mean.\n", n_note(names(ess_labs)))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

- The Own SSS averages 4.4 (out of 10) and family-of-origin SSS 3.9, both below the scale midpoint; in contrast,  children’s SSS averages 6.4, the only one of the measures that is above the midpoint. 

- Wave means move little between waves: own between 4,18 and 4,64; origin between 3,67 and 4,12; son between 6,24 and 6,75

## Social Subjective Mobility

```{r}
#| label: mov-dist-setup
#| include: false

mov_labs <- c(
  mov_dir      = "Own - origin",
  mov_og       = "Own - mean origin",
  mov_exp      = "Children - own",
  mov_inter    = "Intergenerational (children - own - origin)",
  mov_exp_og   = "Children - origin",
  ess_traj     = "Trajectory slope",
  ess_traj_sqt = "Trajectory curve"
)

df_mov <- df_model %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ola, all_of(names(mov_labs))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-ola, names_to = "var", values_to = "val") %>%
  filter(!is.na(val)) %>%
  mutate(val = as.numeric(val))

plot_mov <- function(v) {
  d <- filter(df_mov, var == v)
  ggplot(d, aes(x = val)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = 0, fill = met.brewer("Hiroshige", 1, direction = -1)[1],
                   colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(data = d %>% group_by(ola) %>% summarise(m = mean(val), .groups = "drop"),
               aes(xintercept = m), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    facet_wrap(~ ola, ncol = 3) +
    labs(title = mov_labs[[v]], x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```

## Trajectory slope

```{r}

#| fig-cap: "Distribution of subjective social mobility by wave: Trajectory slope"
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-align: center

  labs(title = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Dashed line: wave mean. Solid line: no mobility (0).\n", n_note("ess_traj")))
```

:::

**Subjective mobility.**

- *Own - origin:* mean +0.48
- *Own - mean origin:* mean +0.48
- *Children - own:* mean +2.0
- *Children - origin:* mean +2.5
- *Intergenerational (children - own - origin):* mean -1.9
- *Trajectory slope:* mean +1.25

- Most of the averages for subjective mobility variables are positive (excepting intergenerational mobility), with the highest being subjective mobility between parental and child status

- The trajectory of subjective social status shows a positive value, indicating that, on average, people believe they have a positive trajectory throughout the different stages of their lives

## Objective social status

```{r}
#| label: obj-dist-setup
#| include: false

obj_col <- met.brewer("Hiroshige", 1, direction = -1)[1]

theme_obj <- theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# categorical / dichotomous variables: proportion by wave
plot_obj_cat <- function(var, labs = NULL, xlab = NULL) {
  d <- df_model %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(ola, val = all_of(var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(val)) %>%
    mutate(val = if (is.null(labs)) as.factor(val) else factor(val, levels = names(labs), labels = labs)) %>%
    count(ola, val) %>%
    group_by(ola) %>%
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup()

  ggplot(d, aes(x = val, y = prop)) +
    geom_col(fill = obj_col, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)), vjust = -0.4, size = 4) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    facet_wrap(~ ola, ncol = 3) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL, caption = n_note(var)) +
    theme_obj +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
}

# continuous variables: histogram by wave with wave mean
plot_obj_cont <- function(var, binwidth, xlab = NULL) {
  d <- df_model %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(ola, val = all_of(var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(val))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = val)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, fill = obj_col, colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(data = d %>% group_by(ola) %>% summarise(m = mean(val), .groups = "drop"),
               aes(xintercept = m), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20") +
    facet_wrap(~ ola, ncol = 3) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL,
         caption = paste0("Dashed line: wave mean.\n", n_note(var))) +
    theme_obj
}
```

# Correlation matrix


```{r}
#| label: tbl-correlations
#| tbl-cap: "Average within-wave Spearman correlations between subjective social status and MJP"
#| tbl-cap-location: top
#| include: false

vars <- c(
  mjp_index    = "MJP index",
  ess          = "Subjective social status",
  ess_og       = "Family subjective social status",
  ess_hijos    = "Son's subjective social status",
  sex          = "Sex",
  age          = "Age",
  ideo        = "Political ideology"
)

df_cor <- df_model %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ola, all_of(names(vars))) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("just_"), ~ as.numeric(.x)),
         across(-ola, ~ as.numeric(.x)))

# one correlation matrix per wave
cor_waves <- df_cor %>%
  group_split(ola, .keep = FALSE) %>%
  map(~ cor(.x, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))

# average across waves on Fisher's z scale
z_mean <- Reduce(`+`, map(cor_waves, ~ atanh(pmin(pmax(.x, -0.999999), 0.999999)))) / length(cor_waves)
cor_avg <- tanh(z_mean)
diag(cor_avg) <- 1

# full matrix (with variable labels) kept for the corrplot below
cor_full <- cor_avg
rownames(cor_full) <- colnames(cor_full) <- unname(vars)

rownames(cor_avg) <- paste0(seq_along(vars), ". ", vars)
colnames(cor_avg) <- seq_along(vars)
cor_avg[upper.tri(cor_avg)] <- NA

cor_avg %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kbl(digits = 2, format = table_format, booktabs = TRUE,
      caption = NULL) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  footnote(general = paste0("Spearman correlations computed within each wave (",
                            length(cor_waves), " waves, 2016-2023) and averaged using Fisher's z."),
           general_title = "Note:", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-correlations
#| fig-cap: "Average within-wave Spearman correlations (corrplot)"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-align: center
#| include: false

corrplot(cor_full,
         method = "color",
         type = "lower",
         diag = FALSE,
         order = "original",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.75,
         number.digits = 2,
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.cex = 0.85,
         tl.srt = 45,
         cl.cex = 0.8,
         col = colorRampPalette(c("#B2182B", "white", "#2166AC"))(200),
         col.lim = c(-1, 1),
         is.corr = TRUE,
         mar = c(4, 0, 1, 0))
mtext(n_note_pw(names(vars)), side = 1, line = 3, cex = 0.8)
```


```{r}
#| label: fun-corrplot-wave
#| include: false

plot_cor_wave <- function(i) {
  m <- cor_waves[[i]]
  rownames(m) <- colnames(m) <- unname(vars)
  corrplot(m,
           method = "color",
           type = "lower",
           diag = FALSE,
           order = "original",
           addCoef.col = "black",
           number.cex = 0.75,
           number.digits = 2,
           tl.col = "black",
           tl.cex = 0.85,
           tl.srt = 45,
           cl.cex = 0.8,
           col = colorRampPalette(c("#B2182B", "white", "#2166AC"))(200),
           col.lim = c(-1, 1),
           is.corr = TRUE,
           na.label = "-",
           mar = c(4, 0, 1, 0))
  mtext(n_note_pw(names(vars), wave_data(i)), side = 1, line = 3, cex = 0.8)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-correlations-we-be
#| fig-cap: "Spearman correlations between decomposed SSS variables (within-person, WE, and between-person, BE)"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-align: center
#| include: false

vars_wb <- c(
  mjp_index    = "MJP index",
  ess_cwc        = "SSS own (WE)",
  ess_mean       = "SSS own (BE)",
  ess_og_cwc     = "SSS origin (WE)",
  ess_og_mean    = "SSS origin (BE)",
  ess_hijos_cwc  = "SSS children (WE)",
  ess_hijos_mean = "SSS children (BE)",
  sex          = "Sex",
  age          = "Age",
  ideo        = "Political ideology"
)

cor_wb <- df_model %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(all_of(names(vars_wb))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  cor(method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

rownames(cor_wb) <- colnames(cor_wb) <- unname(vars_wb)

corrplot(cor_wb,
         method = "color",
         type = "lower",
         diag = FALSE,
         order = "original",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.8,
         number.digits = 2,
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.cex = 0.85,
         tl.srt = 45,
         cl.cex = 0.8,
         col = colorRampPalette(c("#B2182B", "white", "#2166AC"))(200),
         col.lim = c(-1, 1),
         is.corr = TRUE,
         mar = c(4, 0, 1, 0))
mtext(n_note_pw(names(vars_wb)), side = 1, line = 3, cex = 0.8)
```

- One’s own subjective social status correlates more strongly with the subjective social status of one’s children and that of one’s parents, while the association between the subjective social status of one’s children and that of one’s parents is weaker. This suggests that the perception of one’s own social status is more closely related to the perception of children’s social status than to that of parents, which may reflect a greater concern for the well-being of one’s offspring compared to that of one’s parents.

- Variables related to subjective social status show a very weak correlation with market justice; the highest correlation across all waves is 0.13 with one's own status and that of one's family.

:::

- The strongest correlation is between the trajectory of subjective status and mobility between the parent's and child's status, with a nearly perfect correlation. This may indicate that the status trajectory does not take one's own status into account

- The quadratic trajectory, on the other hand, shows a strong negative correlation with mobility between one's origin and current status, revealing a difference in pattern compared to the linear trajectory

## Summary of correlation matrices

Overall, associations with MJP are weak in every matrix: across waves, the strongest are 0.16 in absolute value (log income and income group), 0.13 for own and origin SSS, and 0.12 for mobility (intergenerational mobility, negative). The high correlations are between measures of the same construct: the different operationalizations of education or income, and the mobility measures derived from the same SSS items (trajectory slope with children - origin, 0.99).

# Modelling

## Social Subjective Status (SSS)

```{r}
#| label: draft-modelos

# models with different fixed effects are comparable (LRT, BIC).

df_model <- df_model %>% group_by(idencuesta) %>% 
  mutate(age_gm=mean(age,na.rm = FALSE)) %>%
```

## Social Subjective Mobility

```{r}
#| label: draft-modelos-ssm

## WE and BE main effects of each subjective mobility measure - MJP index
# Same specification as the SSS models above (lmer, REML = FALSE, random
# intercept and wave slope by respondent). The mobility measures are
# differences/combinations of ess, ess_og and ess_hijos, so they are entered
# one at a time (they are collinear if combined), except the trajectory
# slope and curve, which are entered together.

mov_vars <- c("mov_dir", "mov_og", "mov_exp", "mov_inter", "mov_exp_og")

fit_mov <- function(terms, controls = FALSE) {
  rhs <- c("ola_num", "ola_2",
           if (controls) c("ideo", "sex", "age"),
           terms,
           "(1 + ola_num | idencuesta)")
  lmer(reformulate(rhs, response = "mjp_index"), REML = FALSE, data = df_model)
}

mov_terms <- c(
  lapply(mov_vars, function(v) paste0(v, c("_cwc", "_mean"))),
  # trajectory slope and curve models include the SSS index (WE/BE) as a control
  list(c("ess_traj_cwc", "ess_traj_mean", "sss_index_cwc", "sss_index_mean"),
       c("ess_traj_sqt_cwc", "ess_traj_sqt_mean", "sss_index_cwc", "sss_index_mean"),
       c("ess_traj_cwc", "ess_traj_mean", "ess_traj_sqt_cwc", "ess_traj_sqt_mean",
         "sss_index_cwc", "sss_index_mean"))
)

# models 9-16: mobility only; models 17-24: with controls
mov_models   <- lapply(mov_terms, fit_mov)
mov_models_c <- lapply(mov_terms, fit_mov, controls = TRUE)

# model 25: all mobility measures together (with controls). They are linear
# combinations of ess, ess_og and ess_hijos, so the design is rank deficient and
# lmer drops the aliased terms (kept in the order they are entered).
mov_models_c[[length(mov_models_c) + 1]] <-
  fit_mov(unique(unlist(mov_terms)), controls = TRUE)
```

## Social objetive status

```{r}
#| label: draft-modelos-oss

## WE and BE main effects of objective status - MJP index
# Same specification as the SSS models above (lmer, REML = FALSE, random
# intercept and wave slope by respondent). Education and income enter first
# separately, each with its three operationalizations (dichotomous BE,
# categorical BE, continuous WE/BE), then with controls, and finally all
# together.
#
# Dichotomous BE: dummy_educ_mean / dummy_decile10_mean (ever university /
# ever in the top decile). For the categorical measures, which vary within
# persons, the BE is the person's modal category across waves (ties go to the
# higher category).

mode_hi <- function(x) {
  t <- table(x)
  factor(levels(x)[max(which(t == max(t)))], levels = levels(x))
}

df_model <- df_model %>%
  group_by(idencuesta) %>%
  mutate(educ_4_be    = mode_hi(educ_4),
         inc_group_be = mode_hi(inc_group)) %>%
  ungroup()

fit_obj <- function(terms, controls = FALSE) {
  rhs <- c("ola_num", "ola_2",
           if (controls) c("ideo", "sex", "age"),
           terms,
           "(1 + ola_num | idencuesta)")
  lmer(reformulate(rhs, response = "mjp_index"), REML = FALSE, data = df_model)
}

obj_terms <- list(
  educ_dich = c("dummy_educ_mean"),
  educ_cat  = c("educ_4_be"),
  educ_cont = c("educyear_cwc", "educyear_mean"),
  inc_dich  = c("dummy_decile10_mean"),
  inc_cat   = c("inc_group_be"),
  inc_cont  = c("ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt_cwc", "ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt_mean")
)

# models 26-28: education only; models 29-31: income only
obj_models <- lapply(obj_terms, fit_obj)

# models 32-37: same structure with controls; model 38: all variables together
# (with controls). Different operationalizations of the same construct are
# highly collinear, so aliased terms (if any) are dropped by lmer (empty cells).
obj_models_c <- lapply(obj_terms, fit_obj, controls = TRUE)
obj_models_c[[length(obj_models_c) + 1]] <-
  fit_obj(unique(unlist(obj_terms)), controls = TRUE)
```

# First proposal for complete models

Based on separate models of subjective social status, subjective mobility, and objective status, a final proposal for the model is presented. In these subsections, the following variables were selected: subjective mobility between one’s own status and that of one’s children; intergenerational mobility; mobility between one’s status of origin and that of one’s children; and, finally, social trajectory. These were the variables that were shown to have some effect on market justice preferences, and therefore they were prioritized over the others. Furthermore, a model structure is generated that includes two modeling approaches for the objective variables: one using dichotomized educational attainment and income divided into three categories, and another using years of education and logarithmic income. This distinction was made to incorporate the WE effect of education and income into the model, which serves as a proxy for objective mobility.

## Subjective and objective mobility (education and income WE)

```{r}
#| label: draft-modelos-mov-oss

# Same specification as the models above (lmer, REML = FALSE, random intercept
# and wave slope by respondent). Each subjective mobility variable enters
# together with education and income (WE/BE). Order of the models:
#   1. each mobility variable with education and income (models 39-42)
#   2. the same models with controls (models 43-46)
#   3. all variables together, with controls (model 47)
# Children - own, intergenerational, children - origin and the trajectory slope
# are linear combinations of the SSS measures, so in the full model aliased
# terms (if any) are dropped by lmer.

fit_mo <- function(terms, controls = FALSE) {
  rhs <- c("ola_num", "ola_2",
           if (controls) c("ideo", "sex", "age"),
           terms,
           "(1 + ola_num | idencuesta)")
  lmer(reformulate(rhs, response = "mjp_index"), REML = FALSE, data = df_model)
}

mo_mov <- list(
  mov_exp    = c("mov_exp_cwc", "mov_exp_mean"),
  mov_inter  = c("mov_inter_cwc", "mov_inter_mean"),
  mov_exp_og = c("mov_exp_og_cwc", "mov_exp_og_mean"),
  # trajectory slope models include the SSS index (WE/BE) as a control
  ess_traj   = c("ess_traj_cwc", "ess_traj_mean", "sss_index_cwc", "sss_index_mean")
)
mo_oss <- c("educyear_cwc", "educyear_mean",
            "ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt_cwc", "ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt_mean")

# 1. each mobility variable with education and income / 2. with controls
mo_models   <- lapply(mo_mov, function(m) fit_mo(c(m, mo_oss)))
mo_models_c <- lapply(mo_mov, function(m) fit_mo(c(m, mo_oss), controls = TRUE))

# 3. all variables (with controls)
mo_models_c[["all"]] <- fit_mo(c(unlist(mo_mov), mo_oss), controls = TRUE)
```

## Subjective mobility and objective status

```{r}
#| label: draft-modelos-mov-oss2

# Same structure as the models of the previous section (lmer, REML = FALSE,
# random intercept and wave slope by respondent), replacing education in years
# and log income by dichotomous education (BE, ever university) and income in
# 3 categories (BE, modal group across waves; ref. Bottom). Order of the models:
#   1. each mobility variable with education and income (models 48-51)
#   2. the same models with controls (models 52-55)
#   3. all variables together, with controls (model 56)

mo2_oss <- c("dummy_educ_mean", "inc_group_be")

mo2_models   <- lapply(mo_mov, function(m) fit_mo(c(m, mo2_oss)))
mo2_models_c <- lapply(mo_mov, function(m) fit_mo(c(m, mo2_oss), controls = TRUE))
mo2_models_c[["all"]] <- fit_mo(c(unlist(mo_mov), mo2_oss), controls = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-draft-modelos-mov-oss2
#| tbl-cap: "Linear longitudinal multilevel models for the MJP index: subjective social mobility with dichotomous education and income in 3 categories"
#| tbl-cap-location: top
#| results: asis

mo2_coef <- list(
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
  ola_num = "Wave",
  ola_2 = "Wave^2",
  mov_exp_cwc = "Expected mobility children - own (WE)",
  mov_exp_mean = "Expected mobility children - own (BE)",
  mov_inter_cwc = "Intergenerational mobility (WE)",
  mov_inter_mean = "Intergenerational mobility (BE)",
  mov_exp_og_cwc = "Expected mobility children - origin (WE)",
  mov_exp_og_mean = "Expected mobility children - origin (BE)",
  ess_traj_cwc = "SSS trajectory slope (WE)",
  ess_traj_mean = "SSS trajectory slope (BE)",
  dummy_educ_mean = "University education (BE)",
  inc_group_beMiddle = "Income: Middle (BE, ref. Bottom)",
  inc_group_beTop = "Income: Top (BE, ref. Bottom)",
  sss_index_cwc = "SSS index (WE)",
  sss_index_mean = "SSS index (BE)",
  sexFemale = "Sex: Female (ref. Male)",
  age = "Age",
  ideoCenter = "Political ideology: Center (ref. Left)",
  ideoRight = "Political ideology: Right (ref. Left)",
  `ideoDoes not identify` = "Political ideology: Does not identify (ref. Left)"
)

mo2_note <- "Note: WE = within-person effect; BE = between-person effect. University education (BE): ever university education. Income (BE): person's modal income group across waves. Model 56 includes all variables; mobility measures are linear combinations of the SSS measures, so aliased terms (if any) are dropped by lmer (empty cells). Models including the trajectory slope also control for the SSS index (WE/BE), the mean of own, family-of-origin and children's SSS. Cells contain regression coefficients with standard errors in parentheses. %stars."

htmlreg(mo2_models,
        custom.model.names = paste0("Model ", 48:51),
        caption.above = T,
        caption = NULL,
        stars = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
        custom.coef.map = mo2_coef,
        digits = 3,
        leading.zero = T,
        include.loglik = FALSE,
        include.aic = FALSE,
        center = T,
        custom.note = mo2_note)
```

# Proposal for revision @juancarloscastillo

The proposal considers the static (3 original) and dynamic (origin-offspring mobility) variables of subjective status, and the static (categorized educational level and income) and dynamic (years of education and logarithmic income) variables of objective status. 

@tbl-alt1-separate shows the models entered with each status variable to provide context for understanding the following table. @tbl-alt1-combined presents the concept of the final table, showing the coefficients of subjective status with objective status at the same time, and then presents the same series of models including the controls. Finally, a final model is generated with all variables.

```{r}
model_final <- lmer(mjp_index ~ 1 +
             ola_num +
             ola_2 +
             ess_og_cwc +
             ess_og_mean +
             ess_cwc +
             ess_mean +
             ess_hijos_cwc +
             ess_hijos_mean +
             mov_exp_og_cwc +
             mov_exp_og_mean +
             dummy_educ_mean +
             educyear_cwc +
             inc_group_be +
             ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt_cwc +
             ideo +
             sex +
             age +
             (1 + ola_num | idencuesta),
           REML = FALSE,
           data = df_model)
```

```{r}
#| label: alt1-models

# Same structure as model_final (lmer, REML = FALSE, random intercept and wave
# slope by respondent). Blocks:
#   1. one model per subjective status (WE/BE) and per objective status
#      (education, income; WE/BE)                                (models 57-62)
#   2. subjective models adding all objective status             (models 63-66)
#   3. models of block 2 with controls (ideology, sex, age)      (models 67-70)
#   4. final model (model_final), all variables                  (model 71)

a1_subj <- list(
  ess_og     = c("ess_og_cwc", "ess_og_mean"),
  ess_own    = c("ess_cwc", "ess_mean"),
  ess_hijos  = c("ess_hijos_cwc", "ess_hijos_mean"),
  mov_exp_og = c("mov_exp_og_cwc", "mov_exp_og_mean")
)
a1_obj <- list(
  educ = c("dummy_educ_mean", "educyear_cwc"),
  inc  = c("inc_group_be", "ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt_cwc")
)
a1_ctrl <- c("ideo", "sex", "age")

# same formula as model_final, with the selected terms
fit_a1 <- function(terms, controls = FALSE) {
  rhs <- c("ola_num", "ola_2", terms, if (controls) a1_ctrl,
           "(1 + ola_num | idencuesta)")
  lmer(reformulate(rhs, response = "mjp_index"), REML = FALSE, data = df_model)
}

a1_obj_all <- unlist(a1_obj, use.names = FALSE)

a1_m1 <- lapply(c(a1_subj, a1_obj), fit_a1)
a1_m2 <- lapply(a1_subj, function(s) fit_a1(c(s, a1_obj_all)))
a1_m3 <- lapply(a1_subj, function(s) fit_a1(c(s, a1_obj_all), controls = TRUE))
a1_m4 <- list(final = model_final)

a1_coef <- list(
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
  ola_num = "Wave",
  ola_2 = "Wave^2",
  ess_og_cwc = "SSS family of origin (WE)",
  ess_og_mean = "SSS family of origin (BE)",
  ess_cwc = "SSS own (WE)",
  ess_mean = "SSS own (BE)",
  ess_hijos_cwc = "SSS children (WE)",
  ess_hijos_mean = "SSS children (BE)",
  mov_exp_og_cwc = "Expected mobility children - origin (WE)",
  mov_exp_og_mean = "Expected mobility children - origin (BE)",
  dummy_educ_mean = "University education (BE)",
  educyear_cwc = "Education in years (WE)",
  inc_group_beMiddle = "Income: Middle (BE, ref. Bottom)",
  inc_group_beTop = "Income: Top (BE, ref. Bottom)",
  ln_inc_eq_real_sqrt_cwc = "Log equivalized income (WE)",
  ideoCenter = "Political ideology: Center (ref. Left)",
  ideoRight = "Political ideology: Right (ref. Left)",
  `ideoDoes not identify` = "Political ideology: Does not identify (ref. Left)",
  sexFemale = "Sex: Female (ref. Male)",
  age = "Age"
)

a1_note <- "Note: WE = within-person effect; BE = between-person effect. University education (BE): ever university education. Income (BE): person's modal income group across waves. Models 63-66 add all objective status variables to each subjective status model; models 67-70 add controls (ideology, sex, age); model 71 includes all variables. Cells contain regression coefficients with standard errors in parentheses. %stars."
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-alt1-separate
#| tbl-cap: "Linear longitudinal multilevel models for the MJP index: subjective and objective status, separate models"
#| tbl-cap-location: top
#| results: asis

htmlreg(a1_m1,
        custom.model.names = paste0("Model ", 57:62),
        caption.above = T,
        caption = NULL,
        stars = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
        custom.coef.map = a1_coef,
        digits = 3,
        leading.zero = T,
        include.loglik = FALSE,
        include.aic = FALSE,
        center = T,
        custom.note = a1_note)
```

```{r}
htmlreg(c(a1_m2, a1_m3, a1_m4),

        custom.note = a1_note)
```
